title: Motor Vehicle Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
7.     MOS 3531, Motor Vehicle Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Motor Vehicle Operators inspect, operate, and manage medium
and heavy wheeled vehicles in a variety of terrain and weather conditions to
transport troops, supplies, and equipment in support of combat and/or
garrison operations. Motor Vehicle Operators perform operator/crew level
maintenance, maintain required forms, and manage associated tools and
equipment of the medium and heavy fleet. Motor Vehicle Operators are only
responsible for the management and oversite the operations of light tactical
vehicles. Employs land navigation techniques and must be knowledgeable with
the operation of radios and weapons when they are mounted on the vehicle.
Responsible for convoy security and the tactical employment of the 7.62mm
medium machine-gun, the 50-cal machine-gun, and 40mm heavy machine-gun, and
their support vehicle during convoy operations. Responsible for the
organizations licensing requirements and program management.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must pass an audiogram hearing test.

            (2) Must possess a valid state driver's license.

            (3) Minimum height for vehicle operation is 60 inches.

            (4) Maximum height for vehicle operation is 75 inches.

            (5) Must possess an EL score of 85 or MM score of 85 or higher.




                                         3-286                          Enclosure (1)
 3129                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



        (6) Past driving record, evidenced by a search of a motor vehicle
records check, reveals no active state driver's license suspensions or
revocations.

        (7) No more than one yes in the blocks contained in section 6 on the
Physical Fitness Inquiry for Motor Vehicle Operators Form (OF-345) is
acceptable.

        (8) Must have normal vision to include color, acuity, field of vision
and depth perception. The examinee will not be disqualified for a vehicle
operator’s license because of color blindness. However, if color blindness
is indicated, he or she will be given additional training on traffic light
sequence, observation of other traffic, and so forth, which will enable him
or her to drive safely.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Basic Motor Vehicle Operators (MVOC)
Course (A1635X1), U.S Army Engineer School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Truck Drivers, Light or Delivery Services 53-3033.

            (2) Truck Drivers, Heavy and Tractor-Trailer 53-3032.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Semitrailer Refueler Operator, 3534.

            (2) Vehicle Recovery Operator, 3536.

There is a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all staff levels of MAGTF to the opportunity to serve in smaller organizations/units.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
